stories.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy.
Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away.
One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.

stories.title: New evidence suggests spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater
summary: Millions of years after animals first conquered land, some took an extraordinary evolutionary U-turn and returned to the water.
Using machine learning and thousands of fossil measurements, Yale scientists have uncovered surprising clues about which prehistoric creatures truly became aquatic.
Their findings suggest that Spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater, while some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.

stories.title: Scientists discover how pancreatic cancer rewrites its DNA to escape treatment
summary: Scientists have discovered how pancreatic cancer cells continually reshape their genetic makeup to become more aggressive, spread, and evade treatment.
In laboratory experiments, blocking a key gene reversed some of these dangerous changes, revealing a potential new way to fight the deadly disease.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia.

Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.
The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

stories.title: This mysterious mushroom makes people see hundreds of tiny humans
summary: For nearly a century, people in distant parts of the world have reported a bizarre experience after eating certain wild mushrooms: seeing dozens or even hundreds of tiny, colorful humans moving through the real world.
Now, scientists have identified a mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, responsible for these extraordinary hallucinations in China and the Philippines.

stories.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
summary: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System.
Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star.
The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden flaw that challenges 40 years of superconductor science
summary: A superconducting material studied for 40 years has turned out to be far more complex than scientists believed.
Advanced 3D imaging revealed a hidden patchwork of crystal structures, with unusually wide boundaries that may weaken superconductivity.
The discovery challenges decades of scientific assumptions and could explain why some superconductors outperform others.
